title: Unified Inference: Product overview, PRD, design specs, roadmap & pricing (Q2 2026)
author: Maya Patel
content:
Overview

Summary:
Redwood Unified Inference is the product initiative to converge hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployment capabilities into a single developer experience focused on consistent latency, predictable unit cost, and simplified rollout semantics. This PRD consolidates the product overview, high-level requirements, design constraints, roadmap, pricing and packaging notes, and release highlights for the Q2 2026 launch window.

Goals:
- Provide a single API and control plane for text generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private.
- Reduce per-token cost by 20% on average through smarter batching, caching, and quantization recommendations.
- Deliver predictable p95 latency SLOs for common workloads and automated fallbacks under capacity pressure.
- Make Dedicated and Private onboarding frictionless with standardized infra templates and a best-practice runbook.

Non-goals:
- This initiative does not include rework of the existing SDK surface beyond backwards-compatible additions.
- It does not add new model training or fine-tuning capabilities.

Scope and Target Users:
- Primary users: ML engineers and product developers building latency-sensitive features (chat, search, embeddings).
- Secondary users: platform and infra teams who manage Dedicated or Private deployments for regulated workloads.

High-level requirements (MUST):
1) Unified API compatibility
   - Same REST contract for generate/chat/embeddings across deployment modes.
   - Feature flags to enable/disable deployment-specific controls (e.g., rate limits, VPC pinning).
2) SLOs and operational guarantees
   - Hosted: p95 token latency <= 150ms for short-context text-gen (<=256 tokens) on curated models.
   - Dedicated: sustained throughput targets based on reserved GPU capacity; latency targets agreed in contract.
   - Define clear error budget and automatic routing fallback to lower-cost model variant on degraded paths.
3) Cost optimization toolkit
   - Automatic suggestions for batch sizes, cache TTLs, and quantization profiles per model & route.
   - Simulator UI in Console to estimate unit economics under different config choices.
4) Private & Dedicated onboarding
   - Terraform/IaC templates and onprem packaging with documented upgrade path.
   - Security checklist with KMS/HSM integration steps and audit logging requirements.
5) Observability & tracing
   - Token-level cost attribution, per-route latency histograms, error rates, and sample payload traces in Console.

High-level requirements (SHOULD/CAN):
- Canary rollout primitives in control plane for per-customer model version switches.
- Runtime policies for per-tenant caching and KV-prefetching.

Design constraints and trade-offs:
- Backwards compatibility is prioritized; new features must be opt-in.
- Cost recommendations should be conservative: avoid any automated quantization that could cause noticeable quality regressions.
- Fallbacks must preserve safety and guardrails (no bypass of content filters).

Design specification (surface-level):
1) API and Schema changes
   - Add optional "deployment_hint" header to allow clients to request region/capacity preferences.
   - Add a unified "route_config" object in the Console that maps routes to model_family, quantization_profile, and fallback_chain.

2) Runtime architecture notes
   - Smart router: Routes requests based on policy (latency, cost, customer tier). The router consults a cached policy store and falls back to control-plane query if missing.
   - Batching & caching layer: Continuous batching per backend with prefix cache fast-path. TTLs and batch sizes configurable per route.
   - Model variant fallback: When capacity SLOs are at risk, automatically switch to compatible variant (eg. 8-bit quantized or smaller architecture) with routed flag and audit log.

3) Console changes
   - New "Optimize" tab on route pages showing recommended batch sizes, expected cost delta, and QA checks.
   - Simulator: estimate cost/latency for 10k QPS with current settings.

Requirements table (key fields):
| Requirement ID | Title | Priority | Owner | Acceptance criteria |
| RQ-1001 | Unified API parity | MUST | Product | Same REST endpoints for generate/chat/embeddings with documented flags |
| RQ-1002 | Hosted latency SLOs | MUST | Eng - Serving | p95 <= 150ms for <=256 tokens on curated models, validated with perf harness |
| RQ-1003 | Cost optimizer | MUST | Product/Optimize | Console shows recommendations and simulator cost delta, A/B test demonstrates 15-25% cost reduction |
| RQ-1004 | Dedicated onboarding templates | MUST | Eng - Private Deploy | Terraform templates, install guide, and day-2 ops runbook published |

Roadmap & milestones:
- Q1 2026 (done): scoped PRD, prototype smart router, perf harness for p95 targets.
- Q2 2026 (current): API parity work, Console Optimize tab MVP, Dedicated onboarding templates, private deployment packaging. Milestones:
  - 2026-04-15: API compatibility beta and SDK examples.
  - 2026-05-10: Console Optimize MVP + cost simulator in beta for 50 customers.
  - 2026-06-20: Dedicated onboarding alpha with terraform templates and test customers.
- Q3 2026: rollout to general availability for Hosted and Dedicated; expand Optimize suggestions to include quantization profiles and automated A/B experiments.

Pricing & packaging notes:
- Hosted API: pricing unchanged for basic access. Introduce an "Optimize" add-on priced as 5% of monthly usage for customers who want guided cost optimization and extended observability. Add-on includes: extended retention for token-level traces (90 days), cost simulations, and automated recommendation engine.
- Dedicated: introduce two tiers for reserved capacity contracts: Standard (no Optimize add-on, lower commitment) and Premium (includes Optimize, 24/7 support, and faster autoscale burst). Sample pricing examples (illustrative only):
  - Standard 4-GPU reserve: $18,000/month (baseline support, 7-day ticket SLA)
  - Premium 4-GPU reserve: $22,000/month (includes Optimize add-on and 24/7 escalation)
- Private: License fee + setup. Pricing is custom; include fixed platform fee plus optional Optimize license and professional services.

Pricing rationale:
- Optimize add-on is value-aligned: customers pay a fraction of saved spend and get tooling to reduce unit cost.
- Dedicated premium bundle addresses enterprise needs for faster response, guaranteed autoscale bursts, and runbook collaboration.

Release notes (current beta release: 2026-03.1-beta):
- Features:
  - Unified API beta: generate/chat/embeddings supported with deployment_hint header.
  - Console Optimize MVP: per-route batch & cache recommendations and cost simulator.
  - Dedicated onboarding: initial terraform templates and day-2 ops checklist.
- Fixes:
  - Resolved intermittent KV cache misses under heavy tail workloads.
  - Fixed prometheus exporter metrics naming collision for model_cpu_seconds_total.
- Known issues:
  - Launcher does not yet support automated rollback of model variants in Private installs; manual rollback documented in runbook.
  - Simulator underestimates latency for extremely bursty traffic patterns; plan to improve sampling by 2026-05 sprint.

Rollout plan and operational playbook:
1) Beta cohort (controlled): 50 customers for Console Optimize, 10 customers for Dedicated onboarding. Monitor the following metrics daily:
   - API p95 latency by route and model (goal: trend <= target)
   - Token cost delta for customers in Optimize beta (goal: >= 15% reduction for 70% of cohort)
   - Error rates and fallback frequency (goal: <1% fallback events per 1M requests)

2) Canary deployment steps for Hosted:
   1. Deploy router and route_config feature toggle to canary cluster.
   2. Onboard 5 internal customers and run perf harness against curated models.
   3. Enable Console Optimize for internal users and validate simulator outputs.
   4. Gradually enable for beta cohort with 1% traffic, 10% traffic, then 100%, monitoring KPIs at each step.
   5. If p95 latency increases by >10% or error rate increases by >0.5% absolute, rollback to previous router version.

3) Dedicated onboarding steps:
   1. Share terraform templates and checklist with customer success and Solutions Engineering.
   2. Set up staging environment, run installation test suite, and validate audit logging.
   3. Perform cutover with traffic mirroring for 48 hours before moving production.

Ownership, KPIs, and success criteria:
- Product owner: Maya Patel. Engineering leads: Priya Sharma (Serving Runtime), Daniel Park (Platform & Console), and Luis Martinez (Private Deployments).
- Primary KPIs for 90 days post-GA:
  - Adoption: 30% of new Hosted customers enable Optimize within 30 days.
  - Cost impact: cohort average cost reduction >= 15%.
  - Reliability: Hosted p95 latency for curated models meets target in 95% of daily snapshots.

Stakeholders & reviewers:
- Stakeholders: Growth, Solutions Engineering, SRE, Security, Sales Engineering.
- Reviewers: Jordan Kim, Sofia Lopez, Aiden Brooks.

Open decisions (ADR candidates):
- ADR-001: Should the Optimize add-on be revenue-share-based (percentage of savings) or fixed percentage of spend? (Current recommendation: fixed 5% of monthly usage for predictability to customers and accounting).
- ADR-002: What level of automated quantization is allowable in Hosted vs Private? (Current recommendation: opt-in automated quantization only for Hosted; Private must opt-in explicitly).
